Sprinkler review when an existing building changes

Factory F-1 and F-2 sprinkler triggers

Storage S-1 and S-2 sprinkler triggers

Backflow and current sprinkler water-flow data
Check potable-water backflow protection under the applicable plumbing rules. The amendment limits hydrant flow data used for sprinkler design to one year old.
Speculative high-ceiling storage or factory building

For a proposed Group S or F building with a ceiling at least 25 feet high and no identified tenant, review the local ESFR design requirement for Class IV rack storage at the greatest possible storage height.
Sprinkler signals sent to Stickney communications

Check distinct alarm, supervisory and trouble signals and the local requirement for automatic direct transmission to the Stickney Fire Department Communications Center. Confirm the approved connection arrangement with the department.
Outside alarm indication over the FDC
Check the outside audible horn or bell and the clear 75-candela visual device over the fire department connection against the local requirement.
The local amendment requires occupant notification appliances in sprinklered buildings. Record the actual installation and approved design.
Accessible and identified sprinkler test valves
Check that inspector test valves remain accessible and are no higher than six feet above the finished floor. Multiple-riser test valves need identification of the riser and area they test.
Sprinkler floor controls and flow switches
Check approved supervised indicating controls at each floor's connection to the riser in a multistory building, including the locally required floor water-flow switches.
Locating an alarm in a sprinklered building

Review whether the activating area can be readily identified from the approved sprinkler flow indication. The local provision calls for additional smoke detection where numerous rooms in a sprinkler zone would delay locating the fire.

Compare the design calculations and seasonal-low supply test with the exact local safety-factor language. The published wording uses alternative percentage/pressure terms; obtain the authority's interpretation rather than substituting an assumed calculation.
Check that drawings show hydraulic nameplate information beside each hydraulically calculated area.
Check for the outside test header required by the local amendment for a fire-pump installation.
Private hydrant spacing and FDC proximity
Review the local 300-foot perimeter hydrant increments and the hydrant within 100 feet of the FDC on the building's fire-protection supply. Fire-flow review is referred to Appendix B of IFC 2009.
Outdoor access to riser and pump rooms
Check outdoor access to the sprinkler riser valve room and the fire pump room.
Check the local minimum one-hour separation for the sprinkler valve room against the approved construction and actual conditions.

New-building alarm requirement and local additions
Review the local replacement paragraph together with sections 907.2.1 through 907.2.24 and the referenced notification requirements. Do not overlook the locally added sections.
Multi-tenant retail alarm and entrance strobe

Review the tenant-specific activation arrangement and the weatherproof clear outside entrance strobe directed by the department. The local provision specifies a minimum 75 candela for outside strobes.

Alarm panel or annunciator near the entrance
Check the control panel or full-function annunciator within ten feet of the main entrance, or document the alternative location approved by the fire department.
